newsitem.title: GERMANY: Volkswagen to temporarily freeze subsidy payments.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen to temporarily freeze subsidy payments.

text.p: Volkswagen AG said on Tuesday it would temporarily freeze 90 million marks worth of controversial subsidies the European Union has ruled were illegal.

Volkswagen said in a statement that, in an effort to defuse an escalating confrontation with Brussels, it would not draw on funds totalling 90.7 million marks the German state of Saxony wants to give to the carmaker for two plants.

"As a constructive contribution to efforts to clear up the basic questions with the...EU contract, Volkswagen will for the length of the negotations (between the federal government and the EU) not draw on the investment subsidies..." Volkswagen said in a brief statement.
But the company said it would hold off drawing on the payments "at the latest" to the end of December.

The EU approved 540 million marks of a planned 780 million marks in proposed subsidies to VW to build two plants in the state of Saxony. But it says 100 million marks more than the approved amount were illegally handed over to the auto maker.
VW has threatened in the past to take its investment elsewhere if the subsidies are not approved.
